newsitem.title: USA: Sunbeam closes on $500 mln bank credit line.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeam closes on $500 mln bank credit line.

text.p: Sunbeam Corp said Tuesday it closed on a five year, $500 million credit facility with 15 participating banks.
The facility, agented by Chase Manhattan Bank, provides Sunbeam with the flexibility required to restructure and grow the business, it said in a statement.

Chief executive Albert J. Dunlap said "We feel this facility, which was significantly over-subscribed, demonstrates the participating banks' strong support of the company and its new management team."
Sunbeam also said Lee Griffith has joined the company as vice president, sales, and R. Dixon Thayer as vice president, international.

It said Griffith, who will be responsible for Sunbeam's newly centralized sales organization, joins the company from Scott Paper Ltd, where he served as president and chief executive officer since January.

Thayer will be responsible for International operations and will lead the global expansion effort at Sunbeam. Prior to joining Sunbeam, Dixon was vice president, global research, development engineering and global growth for Kimberly Clark Corp and of Scott Paper Co before their merger.
